verdict:
Both stances in the brief turned out to be right, but not where the brief expected.

OVER-REACH — one confirmed, one refuted. Confirmed: `plugins-hardcoded-cn.mjs` had no language gate and no system gate at all, and registered translated partials at `init`, a hook its own sibling file proves cannot read the real language. Filled tables would have pushed Chinese into English worlds. Fixed. Refuted: the DOM channel is genuinely clean. I measured every rule's anchor against 4,238 real files from 295 installed modules + all systems + core; `SPECIALTY`, `{MISSING_CREW}`, `CRT UI Sheets`, `No Stunts Entered`, `minus-btn`/`plus-btn`/`stunt-btn`, `title="Create item"`, `draw-from-table`, `alien-Push-button`, `id="panel"` and `initiative-swap` have exactly one owner each. `NPC?` appears in two other modules only as a JS literal, and that rule is a documented no-op anyway (`to` resolves to the same `NPC?`). All 14 notification near-misses and 13 chat/item near-misses pass through untouched. The one thing the C2 test never measured — foreign *resolution sites* for the Channel A top-level keys — does have three previously-unrecorded owners (core config.mjs:209, and both alien-evolved content modules), all byte-identical strings where the Chinese rendering is equally correct. Recorded and gated, not a defect.

MISSED SURFACE — the templates are clean, the JS is not. I re-scanned all 79 .hbs + 21 .html (text nodes multi-line-safe, plus every attribute grouped by name) and all 62 .mjs + 12 .js with an import-graph reachability pass: the templates hold zero uncovered user-visible English (the apparent `Reset` in alienprgSettings.hbs:48 is inside a `{{!-- --}}` comment; the font names are T-LATIN). The JS side yielded one live miss — CBTracker.mjs:104's `label: "OK"` sitting next to a properly localized 取消, now fixed with a double-anchored rule — plus three items I deliberately did not paper over with rules: update.js's fully English post-upgrade dialog (latent, `updateAssets` is empty in 4.1.13), the Vehicle-inceptions notification behind a permanently-false `&&` guard, and the `! Supply ` debug notification leaking through logger.warn. Writing rules for interfaces that cannot render is how gates rot; all three are fuses now.

MECHANISM — sound, with one real bug. The partial pre-registration genuinely wins: `getTemplate` short-circuits on `Handlebars.partials` at handlebars.mjs:30, `{preventIndent: true}` matches core's own compile at :41, and alienrpg has zero init-time `loadTemplates`/`registerPartial` (the only preload is HandlebarsApplicationMixin `_preRender`, which runs when the user opens the sheet, long after `i18nInit`), so there is no race. `i18nInit` is correctly chosen and correctly justified. The bug was in the appv1 bridge: `html?.[0] ?? html` is not the window root on re-render, and core's own two-root dialog template makes it drop the button half — which is exactly where the new OK rule lives. Fixed to `app.element[0]`.

DRIFT — there was no pin at all; C4 only checked existence and reference, so upstream could have rewritten everything around the four data-labels and stayed green. Now pinned by SHA-256 plus a tag-skeleton hash (both translated templates verified structurally identical to the baseline).

The one finding I documented rather than fixed: creature-header.hbs did not need a whole-file override. Four `DOM_ATTR_REPLACEMENTS` entries would have done it — `dataset.label` is only read on click, and the attribute machinery already exists. I left it alone because the drift exposure is now closed by the pin and unilaterally dismantling a working owner-designed override is not proportionate. The open issue I cannot close alone: 37 of planet-general.hbs's 38 baseline labels (大气 / 水圈 / 重力 / 气候 / 轨道周期 / 资源潜力 …) have no entry in glossary_alien.json, and being hardcoded in a .hbs they are invisible to every term gate in the repo. The new G-group pins them so they cannot drift silently, but they need adjudication and glossary entries before the Core Rules pack translates the same words independently.
